claims.text: Replacing 10% of the ferromagnetic elements in a magnetic high-entropy alloy with dysprosium will increase its coercive field.
At room temperature and standard atmospheric pressure, 10% dysprosium substitution will produce a 30% coercive-field increase relative to an as-cast alloy without dysprosium.
Dysprosium substitution increases magnetic anisotropy in magnetic high-entropy alloys.
Dysprosium substitution modifies exchange interactions in magnetic high-entropy alloys.
The increased magnetic anisotropy and modified exchange interactions caused by dysprosium substitution increase coercivity.
The magnitude of the coercive-field increase may depend on the specific alloy composition.
The magnitude of the coercive-field increase may depend on processing conditions.
The proposed intervention is applicable to material in either an as-cast or an annealed state.

contradictions.description: The quantitative hypothesis predicts a 30% increase, but the falsification rule accepts any increase of at least 20%; an observed 20–29% increase would contradict the stated prediction without falsifying it under the stated rule.

The initial state permits an annealed alloy, whereas the baseline is specifically as-cast. For an annealed test alloy this would not be a matched baseline and would confound dysprosium substitution with processing state.
